now.title: 3.7.2 is out, 3.9 and 3.10 are built
now.note: 3.7.2 fixes a bug that hid OneDrive files from Find my files, and a Print folder wrongly counted as a second manuscript, and it widens Preferences and puts a Preferences button on the library screen. It’s released. 3.9 (Records with the suite) and 3.10 (versions of a record, and web clips from Recon Browser) are built and in review.

items.title: 3.7.2: patch
items.text: Find my files now sees OneDrive files on Windows. A full copy in a Print folder is a finished copy, not a second manuscript. Preferences opens wide, in two columns, and the library screen has a Preferences button so the themes can be found. Released.

items.title: Records
items.text: Characters, places, weapons or your own kinds, with links both ways, @ in a chapter, saved views, numbering and bringing records in from files.

items.title: The suite
items.text: The apps finding each other when installed, an Apps panel, a status line and a book’s word count on request. Webhooks and n8n are left for their own design.

items.title: 3.10: versions of a record
items.text: Freeze a record for each book, with a printable part and an author-only part, canon lock, and records printed as a PDF with a label like Record 0100 · Revision 2. A frozen version can never be changed or unfrozen.

items.title: Web clips from Recon Browser
items.text: Recon Browser sends research to this app over App Link. A clip waits in the inbox, and nothing is filed or fetched without your choice. A locked project holds it until you unlock it.

items.title: Apps status icon
items.text: A small icon on the toolbar with a dot that shows whether other Recon Towers apps are linked, found or off, and opens a panel that lists every app with what you can do about it. It says it in words as well as colour.

items.title: Updates in the Apps panel
items.text: The panel says when another Recon Towers app has a newer version, with both numbers and a button to update or download it. It never stops two apps linking: only an incompatible link protocol does, and then it says which app needs an update. Nothing about you is sent when it checks.

items.title: Looks like the rest of the family
items.text: A Help menu like RT Markdown Reader's with a Help Center and Keyboard Shortcuts, an About window with links and copyable version details, and a bar across the top of the library with Preferences, so the themes can be found before a project is open. Any of the app's shortcuts can be changed, from the Help menu or Preferences. Preferences is now a window with its sections down the side. A tutorial and a find-a-command box are still to come.

items.title: Still open from earlier
items.text: Your own test of the lock and of Find my files, a real Word manuscript, Pages on a Mac, and a real Scrivener project.

items.title: Released before this
items.text: 3.7.2 is the latest release. Before it, 3.7.1 brought the new name, and 3.7.0 RT Markdown Reader on this computer.

items.title: Next, from your own testing
items.text: Find my files sorting by type with a files view and audio and art sections (3.11), read aloud like RT Markdown Reader (3.12), and Connect Claude (3.13), with your choice of how much it may do and a record of every change it makes. The menus, Help and About now follow RT Markdown Reader’s layout, in the 3.10 work that isn’t released yet.

waiting.title: A test and {decisions} decisions
waiting.text: Your own tests of Records and printing on Windows and Mac, a real power cut during a lock, and the decisions below. 3.9 and 3.10 are built and wait for your go-ahead to release.

questions.q: Can the apps detect each other when they’re installed?
questions.a: In 3.9, yes, for this app: it says it’s installed, and an Apps panel lists installed, running and linked apps. RT Markdown Reader needs the same change on its side before the two see each other when closed.

In 3.7.1, under File, then Preferences (Ctrl+,), or the gear at the top right once a project is open. 3.7.2 adds a Preferences button on the library screen. From 3.10 they’re in Preferences under Appearance, which is also at the end of the Edit menu.

questions.q: What happens to pictures in an imported file?
questions.a: From v3.5 they stay with the book as attachments, encrypted like the rest of the project. They sit beside the writing and don’t appear on the page yet.

questions.q: Why did StoryTracker move off WPF?
questions.a: WPF only runs on Windows. The new app is Electron and JavaScript, like RT Markdown Reader, so one app runs on Windows, Mac and Linux. The old C# code is kept in legacy-wpf.

questions.q: Does it use the same themes as RT Markdown Reader?
questions.a: The same set, as copies. It has all of RT Markdown Reader's themes, the old app's Plum, Evergreen, Blue/Orange and Aero, and a new one, Slate, plus Glass with any theme but High Contrast. A theme added to one app doesn't reach the other by itself. Packs, under Later, would change that. RT Markdown Reader is adding a third look, Metallic, beside Solid and Glass. This app copies it once it ships there (v3.23), along with Colour-safe and Customize Theme.
Yes, in v3.22, using RT Markdown Reader's offline voices, with the dictionary's pronunciations. You can already send a chapter to RT Markdown Reader and have it read there.

questions.q: Will the dictionary know how to say words?
questions.a: Yes. In v3.15 each word can carry a pronunciation guide, for invented words and words from other languages. Read aloud uses it, and so do RT Markdown Reader's voices through App Link, so a name is taught once.

questions.q: Can more themes and fonts be downloaded?
questions.a: Theme and font packs are under Later.

questions.q: Were these features taken from RT Markdown Reader?
questions.a: Partly. Most came from what you said you need. In November the two roadmaps were compared feature by feature, and what this app was missing was added: v3.8, v3.21 to v3.23, and wider v3.15 and v3.17.

questions.q: How do I hand an AI a chapter as Markdown?
questions.a: Markdown export arrives in v3.3, App Link sends a chapter to RT Markdown Reader in v3.7 (both apps have to be up to date), and Claude can work with the book directly in v3.13.

questions.q: Can it be tested on real stories?
questions.a: Yes, once the basics work. Your stories and Notion become the test bed, and what you need for how you write goes on this roadmap.

questions.q: Will it make EPUBs that KDP accepts?
questions.a: It makes EPUBs that pass EPUBCheck, the official validator, with no errors or warnings. The test that counts is uploading one to KDP’s previewer, which is yours to do.
